Phylogenetic Tree Inspection and Rooting - meta analysis

Calla Bush St George

2025-08-11

Goals

  1. Load the FastTree unrooted tree.
  2. Add tree to phyloseq object.
  3. Visualize and inspect tree with ggtree.
  4. Prune ASVs, if needed.
  5. Root our tree.
  6. Combine new tree with a phyloseq objet.
  7. Save 2 phyloseq objects: 1. Unrooted tree phyloseq object, 2. Rooted tree phyloseq object.

Setting the Environment

Set the seed

set.seed(238428)

Load packages

# BiocManager::install("phytools", force = TRUE)
# BiocManager::install("tidyverse", force = TRUE)
# BiocManager::install("ggtree", force = TRUE)
# BiocManager::install("phyloseq", force = TRUE)

pacman::p_load(tidyverse, phyloseq, ggtree, phytools, 
               install = FALSE)

Load Data files

# Preprocessed phyloseq object
load("with_pygmy/data/02_PreProcessing/raw_preprocessed_physeq.RData")
raw_preprocessed_physeq
## phyloseq-class experiment-level object
## otu_table()   OTU Table:         [ 6059 taxa and 90 samples ]
## sample_data() Sample Data:       [ 90 samples by 19 sample variables ]
## tax_table()   Taxonomy Table:    [ 6059 taxa by 9 taxonomic ranks ]
# Load in the tree!
unrooted_tree <- 
  read.tree("with_pygmy/data/03_Phylogenetic_Tree/ASVs_unrooted.tree")

## phyloseq-class experiment-level object
## otu_table()   OTU Table:         [ 6059 taxa and 90 samples ]
## sample_data() Sample Data:       [ 90 samples by 19 sample variables ]
## tax_table()   Taxonomy Table:    [ 6059 taxa by 9 taxonomic ranks ]
## phy_tree()    Phylogenetic Tree: [ 6059 tips and 6057 internal nodes ]
# Make a basic tree
kingdom_node_tree <-
  ggtree(unrooted_physeq) +
  # Color by kingdom
  geom_tippoint(mapping = aes(color = Kingdom)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("goldenrod1", "cornflowerblue", "gray")) +
  # Add title
  labs(title = "Unrooted Tree") + 
  # Move legened to the bottom
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  # Add node labels
  geom_text(aes(label = ASV), hjust = 0.5, vjust = 4, size = 1)
kingdom_node_tree
## Warning: Removed 6057 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_text()`).

Prune ASV_3711

# Function from Joey McMurdie: https://github.com/joey711/phyloseq/issues/652
pop_taxa = function(physeq, badTaxa){
  allTaxa <-  taxa_names(physeq)
  allTaxa <- allTaxa[!(allTaxa %in% badTaxa)]
  return(prune_taxa(allTaxa, physeq))
  }

# Let's use the pop taxa function :)
# Recreate a phyloseq object without ASV_4871 and ASV_6441
unrooted_physeq_rmASVs <-
  unrooted_physeq %>%
  pop_taxa(., c("ASV_4871","ASV_6441"))
## Found more than one class "phylo" in cache; using the first, from namespace 'phyloseq'
## Also defined by 'tidytree'
# Intuition Check
ntaxa(unrooted_physeq) - ntaxa(unrooted_physeq_rmASVs)
## [1] 1
# Visually inspect
ggtree(unrooted_physeq_rmASVs) +
  geom_tippoint(mapping = aes(color = Kingdom))+
  scale_color_manual(values = c("goldenrod1", "cornflowerblue", "gray"))

Midroot Tree

# Is the tree rooted? 
new_unrooted_tree <- phy_tree(unrooted_physeq_rmASVs)

# Let's midpoint root the tree
midpoint_rooted_tree <-
  midpoint.root(new_unrooted_tree)

# Assign to a new phyloseq object: merging subsetted phyloseq with the new rooted tree

# 1. Create the phyloseq object
physeq_rmASVs <-
  raw_preprocessed_physeq %>%
  subset_taxa(ASV != c("ASV_4871","ASV_6441"))
## Warning in ASV != c("ASV_4871", "ASV_6441"): longer object length is not a
## multiple of shorter object length
# Merge tree with the new physeq_rm456
midroot_physeq <-
  merge_phyloseq(physeq_rmASVs, midpoint_rooted_tree)
## Found more than one class "phylo" in cache; using the first, from namespace 'phyloseq'
## Also defined by 'tidytree'

## phyloseq-class experiment-level object
## otu_table()   OTU Table:         [ 6058 taxa and 90 samples ]
## sample_data() Sample Data:       [ 90 samples by 19 sample variables ]
## tax_table()   Taxonomy Table:    [ 6058 taxa by 9 taxonomic ranks ]
## phy_tree()    Phylogenetic Tree: [ 6058 tips and 6057 internal nodes ]
# Quick Inspection of tree
ggtree(midroot_physeq) + 
  geom_tippoint(mapping = aes(color = Kingdom))+
  scale_color_manual(values = c("goldenrod1", "cornflowerblue", "gray"))

ggtree(midroot_physeq) + 
  geom_tippoint(mapping = aes(color = Phylum))+
  scale_color_manual(values = phylum_colors)

Save to a new phyloseq object

# Save both phyloseq objects with our tree object to one .RData file
save(list = c("unrooted_physeq", "midroot_physeq"),
     file = "with_pygmy/data/03_Phylogenetic_Tree/phytree_preprocessed_physeq.RData")
